original: branch snapshot/pre-session5 exported to .backups/original_tree; app.main.predict with runs/fmpe_14d.pt (neural OT-FMPE), production_v1 physics
v2: c2i.engine.infer_crater with default assumptions (asteroidal population, three scaling packages, global target unless coordinates given), 12,000 draws per scenario

B_laboratory.description: Holsapple crater database v1.3, dry sand (rho 1.8 g/cc), 37 shots at 1-508 G, vertical impacts, strength set to zero (cohesionless). Predicted transient volume vs measured apparent volume; both models use the regolith (mu 0.41) constants.
B_laboratory.note: Laboratory sand is not lunar regolith; this tests the shared point-source law, not lunar accuracy. The original network cannot be applied to laboratory craters (fixed lunar gravity and a 20-9000 m training window), so only forward physics is compared.

C_real_impacts.description: Measured spacecraft impacts (all hollow, 1.6-2.6 km/s). Forward: same impactor and regolith target (1500 kg/m3, 10 kPa) for the original physics; v2 uses its site-aware target prior. Inverse: crater diameter and coordinates only; v2 also with speed and angle.
C_real_impacts.caveat: n = 5; hollow, slow impactors outside the calibrated regime of both systems. Not an accuracy measure for natural impactors.

A1_original_world.description: Truth from the original training generator (production_v1 physics, original priors), seed 3031. Observation: rim diameter only, except the last row.

A2_v2_world.description: Truth from the v2 declared model set (three scaling packages, global target, asteroidal population). Scored on craters inside the original's 20-9000 m window.

A3_both_misspecified.description: v2-world truth with scaling scatter 0.2 dex (declared 0.1) and 20% secondary impacts that neither system is told about. Scored on craters inside the original's 20-9000 m window.

A_synthetic.A4_note: The original generator only produces craters inside its 20-9000 m window, so out-of-range behaviour is tested on real craters in block C and on the domain flags below.
